clue.text: He's looked on as a professional man

definitions.text: He's looked on as a professional man

parts.words: He's looked on as a professional man
parts.note: reads as a man respected for his career, but the person meant is one whose profession is looking over land and buildings

explanation.surface: A man regarded by others as a member of the professions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looked on' seems to mean 'regarded', but it is literal: this professional's job is to look over property and land and measure it.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who inspects and measures land or buildings is one whose work is looking things over.

parts.note: SW, south-west, is a compass direction
to itch is to be irritating to the skin

explanation.surface: Turning a different way just to be annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change direction' reads as one phrase, but 'Change' alone is the definition and 'direction' gives SW.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap or alter one thing for another.

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary, a communist
an act is a piece of work, a deed

explanation.surface: Writing a work about revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to put text into written form, to draw up or edit it.

clue.text: A page following the nobleman would provide protection

indicators.note: following places the A and page abbreviation after the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A young servant who follows a lord would guard him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing what the thing does rather than a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An earlap is a flap of a cap that covers the ear, keeping it warm and shielded.

indicators.note: using suggests working the letters of others' cars into a different form

explanation.surface: Players travelling in other people's vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestras are large groups of instrumental players.

clue.text: Thanks an artist twice over for depicting a mountain

indicators.note: over here means the whole string so far is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: TA is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: the word twice tells us to write the artist's letters two times

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter is thanked twice for painting a famous peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole string round, not just the last piece; 'for depicting' is only a link, and 'an artist' is the Royal Academician convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical peak in eastern Turkey where Noah's Ark is said to have come to rest.

definitions.meaning: a narrative or report, as in relating a story
a link between things, or a family member

explanation.definitionFit: A telling of events is a recital, and a link between two things or a kinsman is also this word.

clue.text: A vehicle overturned in the long grass went back over

indicators.note: in puts the turned vehicle within the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass-like plant

indicators.note: overturned means the vehicle word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car that flipped over in tall grass went back along its path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses the vehicle (a down clue reads upward), and the result sits inside the grass; the leading 'A' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace steps is to go back along the same route again.

indicators.note: doctors is a verb here, meaning tampers with, so the letters of sent rat's are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe drops and the S stays in; that the letters also run backwards through the clue words is a coincidence, as Doctors is plainly the anagram signal

explanation.surface: Physicians dispatched a rodent's organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like physicians and 'spleen' like the organ; in fact 'spleen' means bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen is ill temper or sharpness of manner, which is what tartness means.

clue.text: Crooked, so could well be in credit

indicators.note: could well be suggests the letters of in credit might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone dishonest might very well end up with money in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked in the sense of not straight or roundabout, as an oblique route is.

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated P
after means later

explanation.surface: Police officers pursue a horse of little quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means small coins, pennies (P), and 'after' is the synonym LATER, not a position signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is a horse fit only for low-grade 'selling plate' races, so a poor runner.

clue.text: Flora has to pedal around before midday-mid-morning

indicators.note: around tells us the pedalling word goes round the morning abbreviation

parts.note: to pedal a bike is to cycle
AM, ante meridiem, means before midday

indicators.note: mid points to the central letter of the word morning

explanation.surface: Flora, a woman's name, has to cycle about before noon, in the middle of her morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a woman's name but means plant life; the hyphenated 'midday-mid-morning' hides two separate jobs, 'before midday' and 'mid' acting on 'morning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclamen is a flowering plant, one example of the plant life called flora.
A melody can be called a strain of music, and stress or tension on something is also strain.

parts.note: a hanger-on is usually a sycophant; here it is literally something of rock that hangs from a cave roof

explanation.walkthrough: 'hanger-on' usually means a parasite of a person, but here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral formation that hangs from the roof of a cave, built up by dripping water.

clue.text: Tradesmen making one start is quite wrong

indicators.note: quite wrong says the letters of one start is are completely out of order

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers trying to make a fresh beginning get it entirely wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationers are shopkeepers who sell paper, pens and writing materials, a kind of tradesman.

parts.note: a disc is a record
over means above, superior in position

explanation.surface: Come across an excellent recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to find something out or come upon it.

indicators.note: free means the letters of respects are released and rearranged

explanation.surface: Paying respects sets ghosts loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectres are ghosts or apparitions, a kind of spirit.

indicators.note: return of means the word of is turned round in this down clue

parts.note: to retell is to recount, count in the sense of telling a tale

explanation.surface: Foresee the comeback of a nobleman once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like the nobleman but means 'tell' as in recounting a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell is to say what will happen in the future.

clue.text: The naughty child may be dressed, but it's unlikely

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
something that may be dressed in a robe is robe-able, spelt ROBABLE

explanation.surface: A mischievous child might be got into clothes, but it seems doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: ROBABLE is a coined word: 'able to be robed'. 'but it's' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improbable is not likely to happen.

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A grumpy doctor receives a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy in temper.

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are put into disorder

parts.note: an item is a short piece in a newspaper, a write-up

explanation.surface: Fail to publish any newspaper report, on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: NO and ITEM, the newspaper word for a write-up, are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving punctually means arriving at the set hour, not late.

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-rate
Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: Intelligent, even if a mediocre Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means intelligent and quick-witted.

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
aches are bodily complaints

explanation.surface: Animal skins have many faults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' looks like animal skins but is a noun meaning hidden stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Caches are secret stores, places where things are concealed.

clue.text: The organisation of chores on a ship

indicators.note: organisation means putting the letters of chores on into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: How housework is arranged aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts, rigged fore and aft.

indicators.note: in manner hints that the answer is found within the words that follow, held in their letters

explanation.surface: Friendly in behaviour, though calm and dignified.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the two words: howEVER SEDate.
explanation.definitionFit: To be versed in something is to be well acquainted or conversant with it.

clue.text: Going round with a Greek character, and indicating a preference for it

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
voting for something shows you prefer it

explanation.surface: A Greek is turning round and showing that he favours it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'and' are links; 'character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivoting means turning on a central point, rotating.

indicators.note: about signals that the law word goes around the street abbreviation

parts.note: a rule is a law

explanation.surface: Legislation concerning sound in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling sound, like leaves or paper moving.

indicators.note: in places the males within the word for principle

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men are adult males

explanation.surface: Accommodation for grown men, in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like the containment signal but is the definition; 'in' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a block of flats or rented dwellings, a form of residential accommodation.
